Admin level and region filter chips

Source: R/filter-admin_level.R
cd_admin_level_ui.Rd

Two filter chips for a page's filter bar: one chooses the admin level (admin level 1 or district, and national when asked for), the other a single area at that level. A page puts cd_admin_level_ui() in its filter bar, calls cd_admin_level_server() in its server, and reads the chosen level and area from the reactive the server returns. cd_admin_parts() splits that reactive into one reactive for the level and one for the area.

Usage

cd_admin_level_ui(id, i18n, include_national = FALSE, show_admin_level = TRUE)

cd_admin_level_server(
  id,
  cache,
  i18n,
  allow_select_all = FALSE,
  show_district = TRUE,
  show_region = TRUE,
  show_admin_level = TRUE,
  selected_admin1 = reactive(NULL)
)

Arguments

id

The module's id.

i18n

The app's translator (a shiny.i18n translator), used for every label.

include_national

Logical. TRUE adds the national level to the level chip, as its first choice and so the one it starts on. Default FALSE.

show_admin_level

Logical. FALSE leaves the level chip out, for a page that only lets the reader choose an area. Default TRUE.

cache

A reactive that returns the dataset, a CacheConnection.

allow_select_all

Logical. TRUE adds an "all" option to the region chip and starts the chip on it. Default FALSE.

show_district

Logical. Whether an area can be chosen at the district level. With a level chip, FALSE hides the region chip while the level is district. Without a level chip, it sets the fixed level (see Details). Default TRUE.

show_region

Logical. FALSE never shows the region chip, so region is always NULL. Default TRUE.

selected_admin1

A reactive that returns the name of an admin level 1 area, or NULL. When it returns a name and the level is district, the region chip lists only the districts of that area. Default reactive(NULL), every district.

Value

cd_admin_level_ui() returns the UI as Shiny tags: the level chip (when shown) and the place where the server draws the region chip.

cd_admin_level_server() returns a reactive holding a list with two elements:

  • admin_level: "national", "adminlevel_1" or "district".

  • region: the name of the chosen area, or NULL when the region chip is not shown or "all" is chosen.

While the region chip is shown but has not yet reported a value, the reactive stops quietly (as shiny::req() does), so what depends on it waits.

Details

The region chip is drawn by the server, so it appears only where there are areas to choose from: never at the national level, never when show_region is FALSE, and at the district level only when show_district is TRUE. Its options are the areas of cache()$subnational_regions at the chosen level, and districts are listed under the admin level 1 area they belong to. Changing the level draws a new region chip, so an area of the old level is never kept. The list of areas is debounced by 300 milliseconds.

With allow_select_all = TRUE the region chip starts on an "all" option, which the server reports as a NULL region. Without it the chip starts on the first area in the list.

When show_admin_level is FALSE there is no level chip, and the level is fixed: "district" when show_district is TRUE (the default), "adminlevel_1" otherwise. Give show_admin_level the same value in the ui and the server call.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# in a page's ui
cd_filter_bar(cd_admin_level_ui(ns("admin_level"), i18n))

# in the page's server
admin <- cd_admin_level_server("admin_level", cache, i18n, allow_select_all = TRUE)
observe({
  admin()$admin_level
  admin()$region
})
} # }
